notes: vigorplus Kotlin holdout: 12 tasks (3 per category) across the camera-communication library, the tire-pressure library and the Android client; answers verified by reading source. Reviewed independently; see vigorplus-REVIEW.md.

tasks.prompt: When a driver taps a tire-pressure warning to acknowledge it, further warnings for that same wheel and fault kind are held back for a fixed time. How long is that hold, and where is that duration defined?
Where is the recurring check that the dash cam is still reachable (and that fetches its status list) implemented, i.e. what runs it every few seconds once the phone has joined the camera's Wi-Fi?
Where is the camera's reply to its firmware-identity query decoded into the release number, the hardware code and the Taiwan-versus-worldwide build marker?

Trace what happens from the moment the phone picks up a tire sensor's radio broadcast until an out-of-range reading becomes a system-tray alert and a spoken warning. Which classes decode the broadcast, judge it against the vehicle's configured limits, raise the alert and produce the voice?

When a user opens a recorded video clip saved on the phone and asks to see where it was filmed, how does the route get from the clip onto the on-screen map? Name the screen that starts the work and the pieces that pull the positions out of the video file, keep them as observable state, and draw the path (leave aside how the phone's media entry is turned into a readable file).

On the camera's home screen, after the camera reports which firmware it runs, how does the application work out which published firmware channel applies to that unit (for example Taiwan versus worldwide builds), decide whether a newer release exists, and finally prompt the user to update? Leave aside how the published release descriptions are downloaded.

Each decoded tire-sensor reading carries a yes/no flag telling whether the sensor's cell is running flat. If that flag became a charge percentage instead, which consumer code that reads it (not the code that creates the reading or declares its type) would need to be reviewed?

When the phone asks the camera for the current state of every setting in one request, the reply is turned into a list of (setting code, numeric value) pairs. If the value in those pairs stopped being an integer, which handset-side code (not the camera-communication library that parses the reply) reads the setting code or value of those pairs and would need review?
If one more camera variant is added to the enumeration of supported camera types, which places that branch on the camera type without any catch-all branch would stop compiling until they are updated?

We want a 10-minute choice in the loop-recording length picker for the newer camera families. Which Kotlin source files must be edited so it appears in the list and shows a readable label (ignore string resource XML)?

A brand-new in-car camera model must be offered when adding a device, and its tile on the saved-device list should show its own picture. Which Kotlin files must be edited to declare its model name the same way the existing camera models' names are declared, offer it, and show its picture? Ignore drawable assets, string XML, preview-only code, and anything about connecting to or controlling the camera.

Drivers should be able to choose megapascal as a fifth way of displaying tire inflation, and live readings must honor it. Without adding a new precomputed value to the decoded sensor reading (convert from kilopascals where the live value is shown), which Kotlin files must be edited so the choice exists, is selectable with a label, converts slider values, and is used for both the live number and its unit label?
